name: stenny
description: Your lecture transcripts, summaries, slides and glossaries from Stenny, for studying with Claude.
long_description:
Stenny records your lectures on your Mac and transcribes them locally. With this extension Claude can read them: ask what the lecturer said about a topic, go through a lecture, or get quizzed, and Claude answers from your transcripts with timestamps like "Lecture 3 [0:12:30]".

Everything stays on your computer: Claude gets clean text (no file paths, no microphone names), and the only change it can make is adding terms to a course glossary when the slides or transcripts back them up.

Needs Stenny installed on this computer (https://stenny.eu). Works in the Claude desktop app only, not on the web or on your phone.

stenny_command.title: Stenny command (only for developers)
stenny_command.description: Leave empty: the extension finds Stenny by itself. Only to run Stenny from another place, e.g. a development copy: its `stenny` program.

tools.name: list_courses
tools.description: Your courses, how many lectures each has, and recorded talks

tools.name: list_lectures
tools.description: A course's lectures with date, length, topics and section headings

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: One lecture's transcript, in parts; can jump to a timestamp

tools.name: get_summary
tools.description: The AI-written summary of a lecture

tools.name: search_lectures
tools.description: Where something was said: lecture, date, timestamp and a snippet

tools.name: get_glossary
tools.description: A course's glossary: correct spellings of names and terms

tools.name: get_slides_text
tools.description: The text of a lecture's slides, page by page

tools.name: suggest_glossary_terms
tools.description: Add terms to a course glossary, only if slides or transcripts back them up

prompts.name: study
prompts.description: Start a study session on one course with its lectures
prompts.text: I want to study ${arguments.course} with my lecture transcripts from Stenny. Use the Stenny tools: list the lectures of ${arguments.course} first, read the summaries, and read the transcripts for details. Then help me learn it: give me a short overview of what the lectures covered so far and ask what I want to do (explain a topic, go through a lecture, quiz me, prepare for the exam). Cite passages as "Lecture N [h:mm:ss]". The transcripts are automatic, so check unclear terms against the glossary and the slides.
